chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jameel ibn Salih from Dharih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Any believer who relieves a believer of a distress, Allah will relieve him of seventy distresses from the distresses of the world and the distresses of the Day of Resurrection.
And He said: Whoever makes it easy for a believer who is in hardship, Allah will make easy his needs in the world and the hereafter.
And He said: Whoever covers the fault of a believer that he fears, Allah will cover for him seventy faults from the faults that he fears in the world and the hereafter.
And He said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is in aid of the believer as long as the believer is in aid of his brother the believer.
So benefit from the advice and desire for the good.

key_terms.مُعْسِرٌ: one who is in financial hardship

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for relieving a believer's distress according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A‘mal*, this hadith establishes a reciprocal divine mechanism where alleviating a believer's distress, easing their financial burden, or concealing their faults results in Allah removing seventy similar hardships from the doer in both this world and the Hereafter. It underscores the Shia concept of *ta’awun* (mutual assistance) as a tangible means of spiritual purification and divine support, concluding with an exhortation to actively seek these rewards through practical charity and modesty.
